import re
p='pathspec/_backends/simple/gitignore.py'
s=open(p).read()
start=s.index('\tdef _match(')
end=s.index('\tdef _ancestor_excluded(')
new='''\tdef _match(
\t\tself, file: str, check_ancestors: bool,
\t) -> tuple[Optional[bool], Optional[int]]:
\t\t"""
\t\tImplements :meth:`match_file`. *check_ancestors* (:class:`bool`) is
\t\twhether to ask if an ancestor directory of *file* is excluded; see
\t\t:meth:`_ancestor_excluded` for why it can be skipped.
\t\t"""
\t\tis_reversed = self._is_reversed

\t\t# Resolve the ancestor directory and the file separately: a file negation
\t\t# only applies while no ancestor directory is excluded.
\t\tdir_include: Optional[bool] = None
\t\tdir_index: Optional[int] = None
\t\tfile_include: Optional[bool] = None
\t\tfile_index: Optional[int] = None

\t\tfor index, pattern in self._patterns:
\t\t\tif (
\t\t\t\t(include := pattern.include) is not None
\t\t\t\tand (match := pattern.match_file(file)) is not None
\t\t\t):
\t\t\t\t# Pattern matched.
\t\t\t\tif match.match.groupdict().get(_DIR_MARK):
\t\t\t\t\t# A pattern can match both a strict ancestor of the file and the
\t\t\t\t\t# file itself. For anchored patterns there is only one match, but
\t\t\t\t\t# `**/` compiles to the unanchored `(?P<ps_d>/)`: on "a/b/" it
\t\t\t\t\t# matches at "a/" and at "b/", and `match` only returns the first.
\t\t\t\t\tis_ancestor = is_self = False
\t\t\t\t\tassert pattern.regex is not None, pattern
\t\t\t\t\tfor dir_match in pattern.regex.finditer(file):
\t\t\t\t\t\tif dir_match.end(_DIR_MARK) < len(file):
\t\t\t\t\t\t\tis_ancestor = True
\t\t\t\t\t\telse:
\t\t\t\t\t\t\tis_self = True

\t\t\t\t\tif is_ancestor and (dir_include is None or not is_reversed):
\t\t\t\t\t\tdir_include = include
\t\t\t\t\t\tdir_index = index

\t\t\t\t\tif is_self and (file_include is None or not is_reversed):
\t\t\t\t\t\tfile_include = include
\t\t\t\t\t\tfile_index = index
\t\t\t\telif file_include is None or not is_reversed:
\t\t\t\t\t# Pattern matched by a file pattern.
\t\t\t\t\tfile_include = include
\t\t\t\t\tfile_index = index

\t\tif dir_include and check_ancestors and self._ancestor_excluded(file):
\t\t\treturn (dir_include, dir_index)
\t\telif file_include is not None:
\t\t\treturn (file_include, file_index)
\t\telif dir_include:
\t\t\t# An ancestor matched an exclude pattern, but the spec as a whole
\t\t\t# re-includes that ancestor, so the rule does not apply.
\t\t\treturn (None, None)
\t\telse:
\t\t\treturn (dir_include, dir_index)

'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

from pathspec.gitignore import GitIgnoreSpec
from pathspec._backends.simple.gitignore import SimpleGiBackend
from functools import partial
for lines in (['a/', '!a/b/'], ['a/', '!a/b/', '!*.txt'], ['a/', '!a/b/', '*.txt'], ['d/**/', '!d/child/'], ['a/**', '!a/b/**'], ['a/**', '!*.txt'], ['*', '!*.txt']):
    spec = GitIgnoreSpec.from_lines(lines, _test_backend_factory=partial(SimpleGiBackend, no_filter=True, no_reverse=True))
    print(lines, spec._backend._patterns)
    for f in ['a/','a/b/','a/b/file.txt','a/b/c/','a/b/c/deep.txt','d/','d/child/','d/child/grand/','d/child/grand/deep.txt','a/top.txt']:
        print('  ', f, spec._backend._match(f, False), spec._backend._match(f, True))
